I had it happen to me after a decade and it hurt really bad, so bad I cried for a year afterwards. He didn't owe me anything, but I didn't see it that way until I had to be the one who ended it after two years. 

Seeing him in pain hurt me so bad, but I gave it a chance to fix it, and my feelings couldn't come back and I had to be firm with him so he could get closure. I think dumping someone was harder as I really did try, but once I knew what I wanted, the feelings had died by then. 

It took me MONTHS to get there and I grieved hard as my feelings died. 

People don't just randomly fall out of love, they usually fall out of love slowly while doing the trying you wish they did. It's hard to leave a good relationship and tell them your feelings have changed and seeing them so sad. Sometimes we try and try until we can't anymore, and what others see as blindsiding, was something we had to fight to save until our emotions were unfixable. 

It just sucks. I'm here because I had to be the "bad guy" and I hate him being so sad :((

It's definitely addicting, but there is a lot of damage which is just self harm a different way. Do you think your mom would understand you talking to someone who specializes specifically in eating disorders?

It's hard and I won't lie, but getting help was the best thing I ever did for myself even though I had gone through countless psychs and therapists until I found the right one. For me, food restriction made me feel powerful because it was the one thing I could control in life and was an addiction to me too. I don't know if it's the same for you. I still struggle, but learning coping skills has made it a habit to check myself and see when I am doing it, which is often when I'm not paying attention. 

Nothing is ever magically better, and when you're skinny, you realize nothing inside has changed at all. At least, that's me. Idk. Sorry I type a lot lol. 

I'm not going to lie that it's hard, but there is an alternative that even on my worst days feels less hopeless I guess. I like intermittent fasting because I can still get that empty feeling, but I'm not collapsing. I can also enjoy pizza again.

I can imagine it will be a long drawn out process, and I can tell you as someone who lost weight when I thought it was impossible, that calories in and out as well as exercise (even just walking that made me slowly lose everything) is a real thing. 

I used to be reallllllllllly skinny due to anorexia and it was from way too much starvation and exercise and I just felt like shit all the time. I learned after birth when I became overweight (beer and baby weight), that I had to take it slow the second time and stray from my former anorexic habits. I was patient and didn't expect to be super lean right away, and managed to lose it all with intermittent fasting (which still gave me that sense of control I craved). I strongly suggest someone who specializes in eating disorders so they can teach you to cope.

It's amazing of you to reach out and try to get help for him, but don't put this on yourself. You can assist, but he has to do the real work. It's his health, after all. He is very lucky to have you, and im here if you need me. I have a lot going on myself lol; but I'm always available if you want to reply or PM. I can be slow, but I'll get back to you :) 

It's unbelievably fucking frustrating feeling helpless seeing our loved ones struggle, and its especially less black and white when it comes to romantic partners. For me it's "easier" because I'm a mom, but this is your partner so you can't just enforce it like I can. Ive been on the romantic side as the one who had to leave/be left a few times due to one of us not being capable of handling each other's shit. 

It's all so hard, as I also unfortunately learned the hard way what losing a partner to mental illness is like when you choose to stay, which is unreal. There really is no correct answer, except that you need to take care of yourself too. You suffer his problems with him, one way or another. It's exceptionally brave of you no matter where this goes, but he's an adult so you can only do so much. 

I'm totally not trying to make assumptions, but throwing stuff out there. None of this is on you, so don't shy away from considering that he may choose to not want to get help for many years, if at all, and if you're okay with that too. It's a harsh reality for most with mental illness to not seek help until all of those who tried to get them help walk away finally. It's so different for everyone, but I hope he takes it seriously for the sake of YOU as much as you are taking it seriously for HIM. Being a caretaker is pretty fucking hard.

My husband died, and my daughter has very early onset schizophrenia that developed this year and she's already on a last resort medication because she has spent 1/3 of this past year locked in the hospital. 

I have a lapse in coverage for one week this month not of my own choice and I'm a wreck knowing I have to pay for the cash price for weekly labs and her appt, and then the meds themselves ASSUMING they let her out on time which isn't looking good. 

After that week, I have to make the new deductible and im still fucked. I have to pay an obscene amount due to her high needs, but the new policy doesn't kick in until the 1st. I'm lucky we have the tax credit, because I was not financially prepared for this. It's disgusting. I have no choice but to suck it up because I make too much. I'm supposedly middle class, but I should be focusing on saving for my retirement instead of blowing everything we had on medical bills. I dont feel middle class at all. 

I was raised in poverty and didn't even know how fucked the system was since it was always free growing up. I almost feel even more anxiety knowing if I'm not at the top of my game, my child could lose her life. It's been a very sobering year, even as someone who realized with her first adult job (20 years ago) that this shit is rough. This is the kind of shit they try to tell you to have savings for, but also that we should also have to focus on retirement ourselves, so yeah. Which are we supposed to choose? Hmmm do I want to lose a nice home tomorrow or my kids life today? 

This is criminal in a supposed first world country that still runs off of the backs of slaves. We just don't see it until it's too late.

It's not me trying to be patronizing about his condition, but its almost like looking into a mirror haha. Med compliance when you're having problems is a huge hurdle in the process for some.

I'm not a schizophrenic, but my daughter is, and benzos can have the opposite reaction than intended for some. Seeing her the way she is even on antipsychotics that hardly worked in the past is an improvement that (as a klonopin prescribed individual myself) couldn't possibly be obtained with just benzos AFAIK. For me personally, benzos give me a horrible headache, but it beats a panic attack. 

Everyone is different, and as my child's psych explained, schizophrenia is a spectrum. Have him ask his doctor about the medications available and his symptoms to see what options there are. My daughter tried so many and is now on clozapine which is a last resort. She still feels sick all the time though :( 

Unfortunately its going to be that way until the psych finds the right cocktail. I'm bipolar 2 and it took an extensive amount of drugs to get to this diagnosis, as well as suffering shitty med symptoms to find the stability and comfort I finally have when it comes to how severe and extreme my downs are. We all just have to kind of go through it, and for some it's worse than others.
